summary.millrose-properties: Millrose (NYSE: MRP) is the only land banker that must publish its book. Spun out of Lennar on 2025-02-07 and run for a 1.25%-of-assets fee by Kennedy Lewis, it had $9.25B invested at 2026-09-30 across 156,729 homesites, 834 communities, 30 states and 22 builder counterparties. Lennar is 63.5% of capital at a fixed 8.5% under filed master agreements; the other 21 builders pay a floating 10.8% (floors about 10%, deposits about 10%, 95-96% of capital in cross-termination pools), but only five non-Lennar names are public: New Home Co (Landsea take-private, about $700M), Dream Finders (Beazer takeover, about $1.07B incl. a $488M 12% preferred), Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI (multifamily) and Rausch Coleman's seller-side holdback. It has reported no builder walk-aways, forfeitures or renegotiations since inception. Its constraint is capital: debt-to-capitalization 36% against a 33% target after $1.0B of 6.50%/6.75% notes and a new unsecured bank facility, and it will not issue equity below book ($35.24), so growth now comes from takedown recycling, a $250M buyback signals the stock is cheap, and the August 2026 amendments opened rentals. Lennar's founder rights (most-favoured rate, capital priority, pool caps of $50M/$25M at risk per pool) shape what Millrose can offer everyone else.
summary.kennedy-lewis: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management manages Millrose and runs a separate private land-banking business with its own capital (Fund III, Fund IV and Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co, 'KLRES'), built from 2021 around a team that came from Domain. It signs builder commitments (New Home/Landsea, Dream Finders/Beazer, Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI) and then allocates them, so far mostly to Millrose; the August 2026 amendment to Millrose's management agreement loosened the rules on how deals are split with its private vehicles. Private-fund pricing and book size are not public; Millrose's non-Lennar yield (about 10.8%) is the best public proxy.
summary.tpg-angelo-gordon: TPG Angelo Gordon's land banking is now branded TPG Essential Housing and sits in TPG Credit Solutions, with a Scottsdale asset manager (AGWIP Asset Management). TPG's own fund decks, posted publicly by a pension investor, claim 850+ projects, $22bn+ of project value and about 150,000 homesites originated with 16 builders in 24 states (about 40% California) and zero losses; the fund ladder runs EHF-1 $1.0bn (2020, Lennar only) to EHF-2 $3.0bn, EHF-3 (deck says $2.6bn; trade press reports a $1.62bn final close) and EHF-4, which held a $2bn first close in Q3 2026 toward a $3bn+ target. Its filed Lennar master agreement and decks show the structure: options under 40 months, a ~20% non-refundable deposit (about double Millrose's ~10%), fixed monthly takedowns, a cost-cap construction agreement with completion guarantee, and a first look on Lennar deals. Option rates are not public; secondary sources put target net IRRs at 13-15%. Builder names beyond Lennar come mostly from county LLC names ('TPG AG EHC III (ticker) ...') and are tagged Inferred.
summary.new-entrants: 2025-2026 brought new, large balance sheets into builder land finance. Apollo launched Olympus Housing Capital (June 2025; about $1B executed land banking per trade press; CEO Andrew Brausa, a Domain co-founder per Apollo's release). Blackstone's real estate debt arm announced a homebuilder lending platform (May 2026; product mix unclear). Blue Owl is funding FivePoint's Hearthstone (up to $1.7B), Guggenheim/Bedrock, Starwood/Trez, and Wafra/Hunt's Strata Land Partners (Nov 2026) all launched land vehicles, and Walton Global, Avila and builder-affiliated lenders (Rooftop Capital, All Pro Capital) publish lot-finance programs. Older names (Värde, Brookfield) were quiet. KKR, Ares and Oaktree showed no public builder land finance. Most of these name no builders and publish no terms, so this is a map of who has capital, not of who has won share.
summary.domain-real-estate-partners: What a competitor or builder can see about Domain without asking. Domain's own site gives scale ($6.7B+ current gross asset value, about $18.2B committed since 2015, 825 projects, 29 states, 91 MSAs as of 2026-10-31), its three products and its team. DW Partners' Form ADV (May 2026: $2.27B regulatory AUM) and the Domain funds' Form D filings show the vehicles and investor counts (Solaris $565M from 41 investors, Metric $333M from 3, Evergreen $205M from 9). The PGIM partnership (over $4B across seven deals by May 2026) and the CIO's podcast remarks (low-double-digit pricing, insurance private placements) are public. Lennar named Domain among its land bankers on its March 2026 call, and Commercial Observer tied DW Partners to a $164.5M Lennar land-bank site in Sunrise, FL (Jan 2026). Most notable for the team: a May 2024 Domain one-pager marked not for general distribution is downloadable without login from insuranceaum.com, showing median rate (13%), median term, monthly net returns 2016-2024, fee model, leverage cost and client names. Millrose's 10-K names DW Partners as a competitor; EDGAR full-text search finds Domain named in only one builder filing (Hovnanian, FY2015).

set.fact: Development funding: Millrose funds horizontal development up to the budgeted contract sum under the Master Construction Agreement; Lennar performs the work as contractor and is solely responsible for cost overruns unless an independent consultant determines otherwise; home construction is outside the funded work. Lennar Corporation backs this with an unlimited parent Payment and Performance Guaranty covering the program, option and construction agreements.

set.description: Closing date. Berkshire Hathaway completed its purchase of Taylor Morrison for $72.50 per share in cash, about $6.8B equity value and $8.5B enterprise value. Sheryl Palmer stays CEO and oversees integrating Taylor Morrison (including Esplanade, Yardly build-to-rent and Taylor Morrison Home Funding) with Berkshire's site-built builders in Clayton Properties Group (15 regional builders). set.description: Closing date. Dream Finders completed its all-cash purchase of Beazer at $33.50 per share, about $2.2B enterprise value; Beazer was delisted from the NYSE. Dream Finders expects $100M+ of annual run-rate cost synergies, will move Beazer communities onto Dream Finders floor plans and aims to bring leverage back to current levels within 18-24 months. The combined company builds in 26 of the top 50 MSAs. Millrose provided about $1.07B of land-bank and preferred-equity financing (see the Millrose profile).

Closed 2025-06-25. Apollo-backed New Home Co, through Lido Holdco, completed a cash tender offer and merger for Nasdaq-listed Landsea Homes at $11.30 per share; about 83.3% of shares were tendered and Landsea was delisted. Landsea's 8-K says the deal was funded with debt, land bank funding and equity (Millrose's own filings show it bought $522.8M of the land; see the Millrose profile). Matthew Zaist became president and CEO; Landsea's executive officers left and its board resigned.
